challenges.name: timeouts-retry-budgets-quiz
challenges.title: Read the payment outage
challenges.description: Three statements about what happened to Rice Rocket's checkout when the payment provider slowed down. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: Count the calls layer by layer: how many times does each layer try, and does every try of the outer layer start a fresh round of tries in the inner one?
Read the thread dump: what is each request thread doing, and what bounds how long it may keep doing it?
Ask what a timeout tells the client about the payment: did the provider charge the card or not, and what would a second POST do?

questions.question:
The gateway retries failed calls to order-service, and order-service retries its call to payment-service:

```yaml
# gateway route (order-service)
retries: 3            # 1 call + 3 retries
# order-service application.yml
resilience4j.retry.instances.payment.max-attempts: 3
```

```text
payment-service  10:41  requests/s  120 -> 1,410   (checkouts/s unchanged: 95)
```

Statement: "Each checkout can reach payment-service at most 3 times, because the payment client is limited to 3 attempts."
questions.explanation: False. Retries multiply across layers: the gateway makes up to 4 calls to order-service, and each of them may make 3 attempts at payment-service, so one checkout can produce 12 payment calls. That is how 95 checkouts/s became more than 1,400 requests/s on a provider that was already slow. Retry in one layer only (usually the one closest to the failing dependency) and give it a budget.

questions.question:
order-service stopped answering although its CPU was idle. A thread dump during the incident:

```text
"http-nio-8080-exec-187" ... RUNNABLE
   at sun.nio.ch.SocketDispatcher.read0(Native Method)
   at java.net.http...
   at com.ricerocket.order.payment.PaymentClient.charge(PaymentClient.java:58)
... 200 of 200 Tomcat worker threads in PaymentClient.charge
```

The payment `RestClient` was built with no read timeout.

Statement: "Without a read timeout each request thread can wait for the provider indefinitely, so a slow dependency used up all 200 worker threads and the whole service stopped answering, checkout or not."
questions.explanation: True. A connect timeout only bounds opening the connection; once connected, a client with no read (response) timeout waits as long as the provider takes. Every new checkout took one more worker thread until all 200 were stuck, and requests that never touch payments (menus, order status) had no thread left. A per-attempt timeout, inside an overall deadline, turns that into fast failures.

questions.question:
The charge call timed out after 800 ms and was retried automatically:

```text
10:41:07.212 POST /v1/charges order=ORD-88213 amount=185000   -> timeout after 800 ms (retrying)
10:41:08.115 POST /v1/charges order=ORD-88213 amount=185000   -> 201 Created charge=ch_7Fq2
# provider dashboard: ORD-88213  ch_7Fp9  185,000 VND  succeeded 10:41:07.950
#                     ORD-88213  ch_7Fq2  185,000 VND  succeeded 10:41:08.301
```

Statement: "A timeout does not tell the client whether the charge happened, so a POST may only be retried when it carries an idempotency key the provider uses to return the first result."
questions.explanation: True. The first request reached the provider and succeeded at 07.950, after the client had already given up at 800 ms; the retry created a second charge. Timeouts are ambiguous for non-idempotent operations. Either do not retry them, or send an Idempotency-Key the provider stores so the retry returns the first charge instead of making a new one (lesson 4).

challenges.name: payment-call-retry-policy
challenges.title: Bound the payment call: deadline, timeouts, retries and a budget
challenges.description: order-service's call to payment-service is a loop in `call(...)` with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: each attempt waits at most `timeout` ms and never past the checkout's `deadline`; only transient failures (no answer, 429, 5xx) are retried, any other 4xx fails at once; retry n waits `backoff * 2^(n-1)` ms, and no retry starts when that wait would reach the deadline; and every retry spends one token from the budget shared by all checkouts (each checkout adds `ratio` tokens, up to the starting amount). The test runner at the bottom reads a policy and the provider's behaviour per checkout, and prints one line per checkout and the totals.
hints: Trace one checkout on paper with the elapsed time after every attempt and every wait. Where can the elapsed time pass the deadline, and which statuses are worth a second attempt?

Look at `Math.min` for the attempt limit, a status check that lets only 429, 5xx and timeouts through, the shift `backoff << (attempt - 1)`, and `budget.tokens` (thousandths of a token: `RetryBudget.ONE` is one) before `elapsed += wait`.

A search client that calls an index with a 500 ms overall budget: `limit = Math.min(perTry, budgetMs - spent)`; `if (code >= 400 && code < 500 && code != 429) giveUp();`; `delay = 50 << (tries - 1); if (spent + delay >= budgetMs) giveUp();`; `if (retryMillis < 1000) giveUp(); retryMillis -= 1000;`.

tests.name: A transient 503 is retried once and the checkout succeeds
tests.input:
policy deadline=2000 timeout=800 attempts=3 backoff=100 tokens=10 ratio=0.1
call c1 503:120 200:80
tests.expected:
c1 ok attempts=2 elapsed=300
total checkouts=1 attempts=2

call c4 429:20 200:30

c4 ok attempts=2 elapsed=150
total checkouts=3 attempts=4
